content.cover_kicker: The slow cooker book for families in Spain
content.cover_subtitle: 30 affordable family recipes, mild enough for kids
content.tagline: You chop, the slow cooker does the rest.
foreword: On weekdays you really want just one thing: a warm, proper meal on the table without spending hours in the kitchen after a long day. That is why this book is all about the slow cooker. You chop a little, brown things briefly, and then it does the work.

Every recipe serves four: two adults and two children. I keep the flavours mild so everyone can simply eat together. If you like it hotter, add hot sauce at the table. You will find all the ingredients in the Spanish supermarket, and most meals cost between €6 and €12.
Dutch beef stew, Spanish lentejas or a mild curry: pick whatever suits your week, switch on the slow cooker and enjoy the smell drifting through the house. Enjoy your meal! – Bianca

Dutch & European.intro: Beef stew, bolognese, cottage pie and creamy chicken: dishes everyone knows and loves. The slow cooker makes the meat meltingly tender and the sauce full of flavour while you get on with other things.

Spanish & Mediterranean.intro: Lentejas with mild chorizo, chicken and chickpea stew and Greek lemon chicken. Simple Mediterranean stews made with ingredients you will find on the shelves of any Spanish supermarket.

World Dishes.tagline: Travel the world, kid-friendly and mild
World Dishes.intro: Curry, teriyaki, tacos and Moroccan stew: the world at your table, but mildly spiced. Someone wants more heat? Just put a bottle of hot sauce on the table.

Fish & Prawns.intro: The sauce cooks gently first, and the fish or prawns only go in at the end. That way everything stays tender. You can buy hake, bacalao and peeled prawns fresh or frozen.

Budget Favourites.tagline: Lots of flavour for little money
Budget Favourites.intro: Simple, nourishing dishes that prove good food does not have to be expensive. Lentil soup, old-fashioned chicken stew and mince and vegetable stew, for €6 to €10 per meal.

basics: Fill ½ to ¾
A pot that is too empty dries out; one that is too full won't cook through in time. Keep the pot between half and three-quarters full.
Hard veg at the bottom
Potatoes, carrots and onions go at the bottom, where the heat is. Place the meat on top.
Keep the lid on
Every time you lift the lid, it adds 15–20 minutes to the cooking time. Save peeking for the end.
Size
All recipes are for a 3.5–5 litre slow cooker. Larger (6 l or more)? Use the shortest time and check sooner.
LOW or HIGH
HIGH is roughly one and a half to two times as fast as LOW. LOW gives the most tender meat; HIGH is for when you start later.
Browning = flavour
Briefly browning meat, chorizo and onion gives a richer sauce. Frying spices briefly in oil makes them fuller.
Less liquid
Almost nothing evaporates in a slow cooker. Use less stock than in a regular pan; you can always thin it later.
Cream and fish at the end
Cream, yoghurt, fish and prawns only go in at the end, or after blending or switching off, as the recipe says.
Thickening
First mix cornflour with a splash of cold water, then stir it into the sauce during the last half hour, on HIGH.
Never frozen
Never put frozen meat or chicken in the slow cooker. Thaw it overnight in the fridge.
Properly cooked
Chicken is cooked at a core temperature of 75 °C: the meat is white and the juices run clear. In doubt? Give it another half hour.
Tinned beans
Use tinned or jarred pulses. Dried kidney beans don't get hot enough in a slow cooker.
Reheating
Reheat leftovers in a pan or microwave until piping hot, not in the slow cooker.
Leftovers
Refrigerate within 2 hours and eat within 3 days. Freeze for up to 3 months; thaw in the fridge.
Keep it mild
Cook mild for the whole table. Put out hot sauce, chilli flakes or pimentón picante for those who want it.
